en-ug-du-an-na: Enugduanna (Langdon En-ū̄g-du-an-na) — first king of the second dynasty of Uruk; EN + a sign read UG after Langdon (the identification is his and uncertain) + DU-AN-NA; Langdon thinks the name may be an error for En-šag-kuš-an-na, a ruler known from another source
[…]-lu: […]-lu — the end of a royal name; only a final sign survives, which Langdon reads LU with a query, and the rest is lost; nothing more can be said of the name
adab: Adab (Langdon Adab) — city in central Babylonia; written UD.NUN plus the place-determinative KI, as adab{ki}
lugal-an-ni-mu-un-du₃: Lugalannimundu (Langdon Lugal-an-ni-mu-un-dū) — the one king of Adab; the name is not preserved on this prism and is restored by Langdon from another copy; the last sign is KAK, read du₃ by sign; the sense of the name is uncertain
ma-ri₂: Mari (Langdon Ma-er) — city on the middle Euphrates; MA + a second sign drawn like URU, read ri₂ by sign (Langdon er), plus the place-determinative KI, as ma-ri₂{ki}; the reading of the second sign is uncertain
an-sir₂: Ansir (Langdon An-sir) — first king of Mari; AN + the BU sign, whose readings bu, sir₂, sud leave the name uncertain (Langdon also allows An-bu and An-sud)
lugal-tar-zi: Lugaltarzi (Langdon [Lugal-tar-]zi) — king of Mari, son of Ansir; the name is in the break on this copy and is restored by Langdon; lugal 'king' + tar + zi, the sense of the name uncertain
[…]-lugal: […]-lugal — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives and the rest is lost
[…]-lu₂-gal: […]-lugal (Langdon '. . . lù-gal') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives, written lu₂-gal; the rest is lost
[…]-bi-im: […]-bim (Langdon '. . . bi-im') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives and the rest is lost
[…]-bi: […]-bi (Langdon '. . . -bi') — king of Mari; only the end of the name survives and the rest is lost
ku₃-{d}ba-u₂: Ku-Bau (Langdon Kug-ᵈBaú) — the one ruler of the third dynasty of Kish, a woman; ku₃ 'pure, holy' + the goddess Bau (BA-U₂), with the divine determinative
munus: woman, female — the SAL sign (Langdon munuz)
kaš-tin: kaš-tin — a compound of kaš 'beer' (written with the sign BI×A) and tin (DIN); in lu₂ kaš-tin-na Langdon takes it as 'wine seller' (the tavern-keeper); what tin adds to kaš is uncertain
-na: -a written -na after the n of tin — probably the genitive -(a)k 'of' (lu₂ kaš-tin-na 'man of the tavern'?); the analysis is uncertain
suḫuš: foundation, base — the SUḪUŠ sign (Langdon suĝuš)
akšak: Akšak (Langdon Akšak) — city in northern Babylonia; written UD.KUŠU₂ (as identified here) plus the place-determinative KI, as akšak{ki}; the identification of the signs is not certain

__broaden__.-ga: genitive -a(k) 'of', written -ga after a final g (unug{ki}-ga 'of Uruk') · locative -a 'in, at', likewise written -ga after a final g, here at the head of a dynasty (unug{ki}-ga 'in Uruk')
__broaden__.-a: nominalizer · locative -a 'in, at' on a city name (adab{ki}-a 'in Adab')
__broaden__.-šú: terminative -šè/-šú — 'to, towards' (the EŠ₂ sign) · the same -še₃ also where the clause wants a locative 'in' (ma-ri₂{ki}-še₃ 'in Mari', at the head of a dynasty); why a terminative stands there is uncertain
__broaden__.ba-gub: ba-gub — 'was set up, established' (gub written with the DU sign) · of a kingship: 'was established at' a city (akšak{ki} ba-gub), where earlier kingship 'was carried to' (ba-ĝen); the city here has no case ending
__broaden__.kiš: Kish — city in northern Babylonia, seat of the first dynasty after the Flood; written with the KIŠ sign plus the place-determinative KI (unread), as kiš{ki} · also the city to which kingship is carried from Mari, and the seat of the third dynasty (Ku-Bau); the earlier phrase 'first dynasty' does not apply here
